pluginJson.name: token-weather
pluginJson.description: A live forecast of the context window, drawn above the prompt: a weather icon, the fill percentage, and a chart of the last turns.

pluginJson.name: context-bar
pluginJson.description: Your context window as a stacked bar above the prompt, a color per category, with token counts and the compaction point. /context-bar shows or hides it.

pluginJson.name: statusline-anywhere
pluginJson.description: Shows your Claude Code status line in the Claude Desktop app. Runs the statusLine command you already have and draws its output above the prompt. Changes nothing in the terminal.

pluginJson.name: burn-meter
pluginJson.description: Live session cost odometer above the prompt: a burning fuse, real-world comparisons, threshold alerts

pluginJson.name: recording-mode
pluginJson.description: /rec before you record: masks keys, personal details, and business figures on screen and keeps private files closed (/rec strict, /rec off, /rec config)

pluginJson.name: reflect-mod
pluginJson.description: claude-reflect as a Claude Code mod: a model check on each short prompt finds reusable corrections (any language); a band above the prompt saves them to CLAUDE.md on one press

pluginJson.name: pixel-cat
pluginJson.description: A little pixel cat that wanders above the Claude Code prompt, watches your usage limits and announces when work finishes; or switch packs for an adventurer who mines, chops trees and fights zombies

pluginJson.name: pixelband
pluginJson.description: Animated pixel art above your Claude Code prompt that reacts while Claude works: seven scenes, or your own image or GIF. Zero tokens.

pluginJson.name: flow-scenes
pluginJson.description: Ambient scenes above the prompt that move with your agent's work: a fire, bubbles, surf, ski, rockets, a hot-air balloon and more, by day or night. /flow to control it.

mode.title: Scene mode
mode.description: auto moves with Claude's work; manual holds the level below

style.title: Scene
style.description: fire: a ░▒▓█ fire with sparks and smoke; warp: stars that speed up to hyperspace; avalon: a colony ship whose shield burns up the asteroids that hit it; balloon: a hot-air balloon that climbs from the grass to space; engine: a steampunk engine that runs up to full speed; falcon: a Falcon 9 carrying Dragon: its booster lands on its legs, Dragon comes home under parachutes to a splashdown; starship: a bigger rocket that hot-stages: its booster is caught by the tower's arms, the Ship splashes down; surf: a surfer and the swell; ski: a skier down the mountain; bubbles: bubbles fizzing up; train: a train through the countryside, faster with the work

idle.title: Scene while idle
idle.description: Auto mode while Claude is idle: a low glow, or dark (the band gives its rows back)

layout.title: Scene layout
layout.description: band: a strip above the prompt; spine: a tall pane docked beside the transcript (fullscreen)

level.title: Manual level
level.description: Manual mode's level: 0 (off) to 10 (the busiest the scene gets)

time.title: Day or night
time.description: For balloon, falcon, starship, surf, ski, bubbles and train: clock follows your local time (night from 19:00 to 7:00); day or night pins it

sound.title: Sound
sound.description: A soundscape for each scene that swells with the work: crackling fire, surf, chuffing steam, rocket roar (macOS only; off by default)

volume.title: Sound volume
volume.description: How loud the soundscape plays: 1 (quietest) to 10; 7, the default, is as it was tuned, each step below it 3 dB quieter. Above 7 the quieter sounds come up most: the loudest already play near full

pluginJson.name: token-weather-usage
pluginJson.description: One line above the prompt: context tokens with their weather, a bar per recent prompt, your 5-hour and 7-day limits against the time elapsed, the prompt cache with its time left, the session cost with the last prompt's share in dollars and in points of the 5-hour limit, and the subagents running. Labels in English, French or Russian. After Token Weather (Anthropic, Apache-2.0) and the ideas of usage-meter (HolyGrail) and prompt-cache-control (Daniel San).

language.title: Language
language.description: Labels in English (en), French (fr) or Russian (ru), or auto: follows LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES or LANG, and falls back to English.

pluginJson.name: cache-tax
pluginJson.description: A Claude Code mod that keeps the one-hour prompt cache warm during breaks and stops a cold send once with its estimated rewrite cost. Warming uses model requests and costs tokens. Requires Claude Code 2.1.287+.

pluginJson.name: filetree
pluginJson.description: An IDE-style file tree for Claude Code that shows what Claude is doing and where in files

activity.title: Claude activity
activity.description: Which of Claude's file activity shimmers in the tree: files read with the Read tool or Bash readers (rg, grep, find, cat) in purple, writes in orange and git actions in green

glyphs.title: Glyphs
glyphs.description: Icon set: auto uses Nerd Font icons when one is installed here, except in the desktop app; plain uses Unicode only

follow.title: Follow Claude
follow.description: on: the tree scrolls to what Claude reads, writes or commits. off: the view stays where you put it and only your own scrolling moves it; highlights still show.

start.title: Open at start
start.description: on: the pane opens when a session starts. off: it stays closed until you run /filetree.

column.title: Right column
column.description: What the right column shows by default: date (last modified), age (time since last modified, short: now, 12m, 3h, 5d, then Oct 9 past a week and the year past a year) or size (files in bytes, folders as disk usage computed in the background). The header button toggles between size and the date or age.

hints.title: Hints
hints.description: on: outside a git repo, a line under the header says git status starts after git init. off: the line is hidden and the tree gets the row.

open.title: Open with
open.description: What a double-click or Enter does with a file. Empty: the default app, also inside tmux. editor: use $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi in tmux (Linux/macOS only; otherwise shows a notice). preview: show it in the pane (left goes back; ↗ always opens the default app). Anything else is a command run instead: {path} is the file and {dir} its folder; without {path} the path goes last. Words split on spaces, quotes keep a word whole, and no shell runs it. It should start the viewer and return; on Linux it runs detached.

edit.title: Edit with
edit.description: What e does in the preview: open the file at the top line shown. Empty: $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi in tmux with +line (Linux/macOS only; the e button is hidden elsewhere). Anything else is a command like Open with, where {line} is that line, for example code -g {path}:{line} or zed {path}:{line}.

pluginJson.name: flightdeck
pluginJson.description: Flightdeck: a live agent dashboard for Claude Code. Main model vitals, an on-call architect, every permission check, subagent cards and swimlanes, a turn receipt and a session log, all from real session events

architectPattern.title: Architect pattern
architectPattern.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) for the agent types and server tools that count as the on-call architect, e.g. advisor|architect|reviewer

architectLabel.title: Architect label
architectLabel.description: Name shown for the architect role

gateLabel.title: Gate label
gateLabel.description: Name shown for the permission panel

panels.title: Panels
panels.description: Comma-separated panels in display order: main, architect, gate, agents, loops, receipt, log. Leave one out to hide it.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Animate the connectors while real work flows, or keep them still

moments.title: Architect moments
moments.description: Show the inferred moment of each consult (before a plan, error repeats, before done)

matchDescriptions.title: Match agent descriptions
matchDescriptions.description: Also count an agent type as the architect when its description (not just its name) matches the pattern

maxCards.title: Cards before swimlanes
maxCards.description: Agent cards drawn side by side; more agents than this switch to swimlanes (1-6)

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: auto: a summary of at most 8 rows when the pane sits inline above the prompt, two columns from 110 columns when docked, one column otherwise

palette.title: Palette
palette.description: theme follows your Claude Code theme (light, dark, colour-blind); pastel is fixed colours tuned for dark terminals

openOnStart.title: Open on start
openOnStart.description: Open the pane when a session starts

statusLine.title: Status line
statusLine.description: Show context, agents, consults and denials in the status line

pluginJson.name: prismantis
pluginJson.description: Colorful, themeable rendering for Claude Code replies: tables, headings, code, numbers, paths and links.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Draw replies with this mod. Off falls back to Claude Code's own renderer.

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: Base palette, from popular MIT-licensed themes. Light variants: catppuccin-latte, gruvbox-light, rose-pine-dawn, github-light, solarized-light. mono uses bold and dim only. random picks a dark color preset each time the mod loads (session start or reload).

headingStyle.title: Heading style
headingStyle.description: Terminals have one font size, so headings get weight instead: banner (a box around H1, a heavy rule under H2), bold, underline, or uppercase H1.

tableStyle.title: Table style
tableStyle.description: box: every cell boxed, with a double line under the header. rules: a rule under the header and between rows. grid: heavier header rule, wider gaps. minimal: header rule only.

promptStyle.title: Your prompt style
promptStyle.description: How the prompts you type draw in the transcript. bubble: a rounded box in the accent color. bar: an accent bar on the left. chevron: a bold accent › before the text. off: Claude Code's own look.

clock.title: Clock times
clock.description: Shows when you sent each prompt and when each turn finished. 24h: 14:32. 12h: 2:32 PM. A time from another day gets its date. off: no times.

toolStyle.title: Tool row style
toolStyle.description: How tool rows (Ran, Read, Edited) sit next to Claude's sentences. chat: tool rows dimmed on the right, Claude on the left. tree-dim: tucked under the sentence with ⎿ and dimmed. tree-bold: tree-dim plus one-line sentences in bold. classic: the original look.

toolOutput.title: Tool output
toolOutput.description: How much of a tool call shows. full: what Claude Code shows. quiet: rows say in plain words what a call did, reads, searches and listings show only their row, other shell commands show their first lines, edits keep their diff, a failed call shows the last line of its error, and a refused call its full reason. Needs toolRows on.

taskStyle.title: Task list style
taskStyle.description: How - [ ] and - [x] items draw. checks: [ ] and [✓] with done items dimmed and struck through. ticks: ○ and ✓, done items dimmed. box: □ and ✓, done items dimmed and struck through. progress: ticks with a done-count bar above each list.

rtl.title: Right-to-left terminal
rtl.description: Hebrew and Arabic get a right-to-left layout (right aligned, bullets and quote bars on the right, tables mirrored), with the letters sent the way your terminal needs them. auto detects the terminal; pick one to force its handling, or off for none.

highlightNumbers.title: Highlight numbers
highlightNumbers.description: Color versions, IDs, counts and durations in prose and tables.

accentColor.title: Accent
accentColor.description: Color for the reply bullet, H3+ headings and quote bars. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

headingColor.title: Heading
headingColor.description: Color for H1 and H2 headings. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

tableHeaderColor.title: Table header
tableHeaderColor.description: Color for table header cells. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

tableRuleColor.title: Table rule
tableRuleColor.description: Color for table rules. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

numberColor.title: Numbers
numberColor.description: Color for versions, IDs and counts. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

pathColor.title: Paths
pathColor.description: Color for file paths. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

linkColor.title: Links
linkColor.description: Color for links and URLs. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

inlineCodeColor.title: Inline code
inlineCodeColor.description: Color for `inline code`. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

codeCommandColor.title: Code command
codeCommandColor.description: Color for the command word in shell blocks. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

codeFlagColor.title: Code flag
codeFlagColor.description: Color for --flags in shell blocks. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

codeStringColor.title: Code string
codeStringColor.description: Color for quoted strings in shell blocks. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

strongColor.title: Bold text
strongColor.description: Color for **bold** text. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

quoteColor.title: Quote
quoteColor.description: Color for block quotes. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

mermaidAscii.title: Mermaid ASCII only
mermaidAscii.description: Draw diagrams with + - | > instead of box-drawing characters, for fonts without them.

diagramColor.title: Diagram lines
diagramColor.description: Color for diagram boxes and arrows. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

diagramTextColor.title: Diagram text
diagramTextColor.description: Color for diagram labels and LaTeX formulas. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

toolRows.title: Tool rows
toolRows.description: Draw tool calls as one compact line: Ran gh pr view 12, Read ~/src/app.ts, Edited README.md. Results still draw below as usual.

emphasisColor.title: Italic text
emphasisColor.description: Color for *italic* text. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

codeTextColor.title: Code text
codeTextColor.description: Color for code block text. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

codeCommentColor.title: Code comment
codeCommentColor.description: Color for # comments in shell blocks. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

ruleColor.title: Rules
ruleColor.description: Color for horizontal rules, diff card borders and chart gridlines. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

bulletColor.title: Bullets
bulletColor.description: Color for list bullets and numbers. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

diffAddedColor.title: Diff added
diffAddedColor.description: Color for added diff lines: their + marks and count, and in hex the tint behind them, mixed into black or white so code text stays at 4.5:1. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme's green.

diffRemovedColor.title: Diff removed
diffRemovedColor.description: Color for removed diff lines: their - marks and count, and in hex the tint behind them, mixed into black or white so code text stays at 4.5:1. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme's red.

diffStyle.title: Diff style
diffStyle.description: How edit and shell edit diffs draw. card: a rounded box with tinted lines. full: no box, each changed line tinted across the width. marks: no box and no tint, changed lines in the theme's diff colors. bar: no box and no tint, a colored ▌ before each changed line.

mermaid.title: Mermaid diagrams
mermaid.description: Draw ```mermaid blocks as colored box art sized to the terminal. Off leaves the code as written.

copyButtons.title: Copy buttons
copyButtons.description: Put a copy button on code blocks, tables, diagrams, lists and quotes. Reach them with ctrl+x tab then Enter, or click where the terminal passes clicks through.

copyButtonStyle.title: Copy button style
copyButtonStyle.description: inline: buttons beside or above each block, always shown. hover: a block's buttons float over its top-right corner only while the pointer is over it, and the reply's over its bottom-right corner, so they take no line; ctrl+x tab does not reach them, and the mobile app, which has no pointer, shows them inline. Needs copyButtons on.

issueHint.title: Issue hint
issueHint.description: On your first prompt and every tenth after it, tell the model it can offer, after asking you, to open a minimal repro issue on prismantis when you say something drew wrong. About 35 tokens each time.

diagramHints.title: Diagram hints
diagramHints.description: Attach a short note, read by the model and never shown, to each prompt you type or another plugin sends, saying tables, code, mermaid diagrams, charts and figures render here, and LaTeX formulas when the renderer runs. About 630 tokens per prompt (about 275 for the main part, about 360 for figures), about 80 more with LaTeX. Off when mermaid is off.

latex.title: LaTeX math
latex.description: Draw $$ and ```math formulas as typeset images in kitty and Ghostty (not under tmux) with RaTeX's renderer, installed as ratex-render on your PATH. Off runs nothing. Formulas that can't be drawn stay as text.

pluginJson.name: ctx-handoff
pluginJson.description: Turns what you teach Claude into project notes, catches its usual slips, keeps the cache warm while you're away, and picks long sessions back up

pluginJson.name: after
pluginJson.description: A real prompt queue for Claude Code: /after <task> runs it after the current task, without steering. See, reorder and remove queued tasks from a band and a live pane, in plain language.

smart.title: Plain-language commands
smart.description: Ask a small model what a command means when it may refer to queued tasks ("remove the tests one"). Off: local matching only.

model.title: Model for plain-language commands
model.description: An alias (haiku) or a full model id.

display.title: Where the queue shows
display.description: band: above the prompt · status: one line under it · none: only /after and /after watch

pluginJson.name: sub-meter
pluginJson.description: Your subscription usage at the bottom right of Claude Code: the 5-hour and weekly windows, as a bar that takes turns.

hideCycleHint.title: Hide the mode cycle hint
hideCycleHint.description: Drop "(shift+tab to cycle)" after the permission mode, to leave room for the meter.

pluginJson.name: token-meter
pluginJson.description: Each turn's tokens and the session's running total, in color at the end of the hint line under the prompt.

pluginJson.name: use-haiku
pluginJson.description: Start a prompt with _ and that turn runs on Haiku, shown as you type, while it runs and under the answer.
